body:
Every elementwise kernel measured (the emulator's own `scale` and `residual_add`, and Qwen's
`binary_mul_col`) spends five instruction words per 128-element row (load; multiply + accumulate; store;
counters; branch), so the multiplier works 20% of the time.

The timing contract already allows one word per row: LOAD reads LRs after the word's LR writes, MULT
reads its registers at cycle start (so it multiplies the previous word's load), ACC/AAQ take this word's
results, and the LR sub-slots and the branch read cycle-start LRs.

Measured on the emulator, no ISA change:
- `scale` (y = x*s, 128 rows): 642 -> 132 cycles (4.9x), multiplier 20% -> 97%.
- Qwen's `binary_mul_col` (87 cases, e4/e5/dynamic, hardware-clean): 1302 -> 280 cycles (4.65x), 20% -> 91%.

Caveat: the last iteration loads one row past the input (harmless unless the input ends XMEM).
The agent prompt now has this pattern (harness change, 2026-11-10).
title: Elementwise loops run at 5 words per row; the timing contract allows 1

body:
Multiplier utilisation on the emulator (largest cases):

| kernel | Qwen | emulator's own |
|---|---|---|
| gemm | 94-98% | matmul_x128_c2 95.5%, matmul_small 46%, fully_connected 48% |
| row softmax | 36% (4096x256) | softmax_rows_long 10-11%, softmax_rows_partial 1-6% |
| layernorm | 15-24% | layernorm 46% |
| elementwise mul | 20% | scale / residual_add 20% (both pipelinable to ~95%) |

Qwen's gemm matches the best hand-written matmul and its softmax beats the emulator's; its layernorm is
about half as efficient as the emulator's. (The gemm, softmax and layernorm numbers come from attempts the
harness wrongly rejected; those kernels are being rewritten.)
title: Qwen's kernels vs the emulator's known-good kernels (MobileViT visit)
